help_topics.title: Understanding receipt and yard links
help_topics.business_question: Why can a receipt trailer link change automatically?
help_topics.plain_answer: Three triggers maintain receipt-to-yard links. Receipt insertion links matching yard rows with coded status 0. An update targeting the trailer ID refreshes that link and can clear it when no matching yard row exists. A newly inserted yard record can attach existing unlinked receipts, but uses a different status rule.

Trailer-column UPDATE uses a left join, so a missing match clears the yard ID.
Yard insertion attaches matching unlinked receipts except trailing status 900, without testing inserted yard status.

help_topics.title: Understanding accessorial identifier normalization

help_topics.plain_answer: Yes. When an inserted or updated accessorial has a negative internal number, the trigger normalizes negative rows sharing its computed shipment-or-container association. The target scope can include existing rows with that association, not just the newly inserted IDs.

help_topics.title: Understanding locating rule retrieval
help_topics.business_question: Does retrieving an active locating rule put stock away?
help_topics.plain_answer: No. This helper only returns the header matching a rule name, including inactive headers. AIM describes locating as selecting storage destinations using rule sequences and strategies; physical putaway and work creation require additional processing. Delayed locating also depends on the receiving preference.

help_topics.title: Understanding action-to-status mapping
help_topics.business_question: Why can a status lookup return no status?
help_topics.plain_answer: The helper maps an action through generic configuration to a system-status identity, then to a numeric status in the requested functional area. Missing mappings yield NULL. Multiple qualifying status rows are assigned without ordering. It does not validate an individual transaction's permitted next step.

semantic_contracts.purpose: Propagate supplied ship-confirm status across shipment, detail, containers and load, and enqueue matching alerts.
inputs_defaults: shipNum numeric(9), loadNum numeric(9), newSts numeric(3), stsLimit numeric(3); all required, no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: No explicit validation that loadNum belongs to shipNum, that newSts is an allowed transition, or that stsLimit is suitable. NULL IDs match no equality rows but other independently scoped statements can still run.

newSts targets nonnullable status columns; NULL can fail. stsLimit NULL makes its comparisons unknown. Nullable historical quantities can propagate NULL during addition into nonnullable QUANTITY_AT_STS1 and fail. No ISNULL normalization is applied to those included quantities.
MIN over no linked shipment returns NULL; the target load schema/caller controls whether that value is acceptable. Detail rows at numeric 995 are excluded while header/container updates are not.
output_shape: No intentional SELECT result set or explicit result code. Assignment SELECTs populate local variables. Affected-row messages are not suppressed by this body.

ordered_branches.explanation: Insert unprocessed alert requests for matching active alert definitions when shipment trailing status is NULL or less than newSts and no matching alert/source/new-status request is visible. Alert reads use NOLOCK.

Read shipment warehouse and set header leading/trailing status to the supplied newSts, actual ship/stamp timestamps to UTC now and status dates to the warehouse-local calendar date. This UPDATE does not repeat the advancing-status guard used by alert insertion.
For detail rows with status1>=stsLimit except status1=995, shift ten-slot status/quantity history one slot right and set first-slot quantity to zero.
For all detail rows except status1=995, set status1 to newSts and add quantities from slots 2..10 whose statuses are below stsLimit.

Re-evaluate status1<>995 after the preceding UPDATE assigned newSts. For rows still matching, locate the first slot from 2..10 whose status reaches the limit and shift that slot and following suffix forward; zero unused tail slots and stamp the row. If the caller supplied newSts=995, this compaction UPDATE skips rows just assigned 995. This is a suffix-selection algorithm, not an independent filter of every later slot.
